title: Free Speech and Artificial Intelligence
abstract: arXiv:2608.28973v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Philosophers and legal scholars are engaged in debates about the implications of artificial intelligence for freedom of expression. This paper analyzes the free speech issues raised by two distinct AI technologies: social media recommendation algorithms and conversational AI (i.e., chatbots powered by large language models). The first part shows that, through their recommendation algorithms, social media platforms control the dynamics of speech visibility in the digital public sphere, making algorithmic recommendation relevant to the philosophy of free speech. The second part turns to conversational AI. It discusses both the reasons for granting or withholding speech rights to artificial agents and users' right to receive information, which may render specific forms of chatbot regulation illegitimate. translated_abstract: 哲学家和法学学者正就人工智能对言论自由的影响展开辩论。本文分析了两种不同人工智能技术所引发的言论自由问题：社交媒体推荐算法和对话式人工智能（即由大语言模型驱动的聊天机器人）。第一部分表明，社交媒体平台通过其推荐算法控制着数字公共领域中言论可见度的动态变化，从而使算法推荐与言论自由哲学产生关联。第二部分转向对话式人工智能，讨论了授予或不授予人工代理言论权的理由，以及用户接收信息的权利——这一权利可能使某些形式的聊天机器人监管失去正当性。贯穿全文，本章还探讨了社交媒体平台或人工智能开发者是否拥有企业言论权。其总体目标在于……
tldr: 本文系统分析了社交媒体推荐算法与对话式AI引发的言论自由问题，指出平台通过算法控制言论可见度，并论证用户接收信息的权利可能使某些聊天机器人监管失去正当性。
en_tdlr: This paper analyzes free speech issues raised by social media recommendation algorithms and conversational AI, showing that platforms control speech visibility through algorithms and that users' right to receive information may render certain chatbot regulations illegitimate.
